newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice not traded after open interest fall.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice not traded after open interest fall.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures did not trade on Wednesday, because investors lost interest in trading after continuous falls of open interest, traders said.
They said that investors had liquidated most of their positions and moved their money to the more active stock market over the past few days.
"Open interest of rice contracts has fallen to a very low level, which indicated that most investors have lost interest in the rice market," one trader said.
The open interest of the October 1996 contract was 1,370 lots and of December was 1,790 on Tuesday. One lot is five tonnes.
"Most retail investors are afraid of more losses because they have lost heavily in the September contract, whose trading has been dominated by institutions," he added. "The market is too small."
Traders said that volume would be very thin even if rice trades in the next few days.
